neighbours.label: 'in'/'into' right after 'get' in a get-in idiom (get in the habit, get into, get in touch, get in here)
fire: If you want to stay fit, try to get in the habit of walking after dinner.
New volunteers should get in touch with the coordinator before Friday.
It took me years to get into the routine of writing every morning.
Kids, get in the car or we will miss the start of the film.
The coach told his players to get in position before the kick.
She finally managed to get into the habit of saving a little each month.
If anything goes wrong, get in contact with the front desk.
We had to get in line early to buy tickets for the show.
quiet: If you want to stay fit, try walking in the park after dinner.
New volunteers should arrive in the office before Friday.
It took me years to enjoy writing in the morning.
Kids, sit quietly in the back or we will miss the start of the film.
The coach told his players to stand in a circle before the kick.
She finally managed to get a little money saved each month.
If anything goes wrong, call the front desk in the lobby.
We had to get tickets early to see the show.

notes: Card: ' in' x20, ' into' x5, all top six right after 'get' (get in the habit, get into the habit, get in contact). The - pole is 'get [one's] hands on'. Near misses keep 'in' after other verbs and 'get' with other words.
